McLaren: McLaren has reshaped the front and rear corners of the car and tweaked the diffuser’s shape to smooth out the airflow around the chassis. These changes give the car a tighter, more stable grip through high‑speed corners and a cleaner wake off the back, meaning better tyre wear and more consistent lap times. In short, the car should feel more predictable on the track and be able to push harder for longer during this weekend’s sessions.
Mercedes F1 Team: Mercedes F1 Team did not submit any updates for this event.
Red Bull Racing: Red Bull has added a small “vane” to the lower part of the front wing, which helps smooth the air around the front tyres and gives the car a little extra bite into the corners. They’ve also tweaked the rubber‑filled seal on the front‑corner bar, making it more durable so the aero‑load stays consistent throughout the stint. Together, the changes should translate into tighter turn‑in, more stable handling and less risk of a sudden loss of grip during this weekend’s race.
Scuderia Ferrari: Ferrari has given the car’s under‑floor a tidy makeover – the front‑floor edge, the board braces and the diffuser have all been reshaped and their internal volumes tweaked, while the side‑pod inlet has been widened and its lower‑volume “coke‑line” area re‑profiled. Those changes smooth the airflow under the car, giving a bit more rear down‑force and a steadier balance, which should translate into better grip through the high‑speed corners of this weekend’s circuit. In short, the updates aim to make the car stick to the asphalt more consistently, giving the team a fighting chance at a stronger qualifying and race performance.
Racing Bulls / RB: Racing Bulls has freshened up the car’s aero package – a revised front‑wing endplate, new rear‑wing flaps, and a reshaped engine‑cover shoulder all work together to clean up the airflow over the car.  A suite of floor updates – new leading‑edge devices, a fresh floor board and re‑profiled floor edge – plus a redesigned front‑brake duct and mirror stay, boost downforce and keep the tyres and brakes at optimal temperature.  The net result should be more grip and a quicker lap time right out of the box for this weekend’s race.
Aston Martin: Aston Martin did not submit any updates for this event.
Alpine F1 Team: Alpine has given the back of the car a quick makeover – the rear‑floor corner has been reshaped and the rear‑wing flap has been re‑profiled. These tweaks tighten up the airflow over the diffuser and wing, giving the car a little extra grip and stability in the high‑speed corners. In short, the changes should help the team extract more pace and keep the car balanced as the rubber builds up this weekend.
Cadillac: Cadillac has tweaked the shape of its front‑floor fence to smooth out airflow under the car, giving the chassis a cleaner “suction” effect that translates to better grip through the corners. They’ve also reshaped the side‑pod cooling vents on the roof‑deck, letting the engine stay cooler without sacrificing aerodynamic efficiency. Together, these changes should help the Cadillac run faster through high‑speed sections and keep the power unit humming strong all weekend.
